newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 19.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* General Motors Corp is looking to build a small, low-priced car in Brazil.
* Sun Microsystems Inc plans to sell encryption softare from a Russian supplier to overseas firms.
* E.W. Scripps has agreed to buy the media assets of Harte-Hanks Communications Inc for as much as $775 million.
* Housing starts climbed 2.6 percent in April.
* Japan's trade surplus more than doubled in April.
* Two Florida electric plans have filed for bankruptcy protection.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dropped 138.88 to 7194.67 points.
* Trades processed by Bear Stearns Cos Inc for defunct A.R. Baron is under investigation by federal and state authorities, unnamed sources said.
* The failure of SBC Communications Inc to secure the Justice Department's endorsement to offer long-distance service means local phone companies face tough obstacles in entering the market.
* Aetna Inc President Joseph Sebastianelli quit after just nine weeks on the job.
* Chevron Corp and a group of other companies have signed a $2 billion pipeline deal in Russia.
* Mazda Motor Corp plans to trim its U.S. dealership network, unnamed sources said.
* Northern States Power Co and Wisconsin Energy Corp have called off their merger.
* Oracle Corp has agreed to buy a unit of Netscape Communications Corp that develops Internet browsing software.
* A unit of Dean Witter Discover & Co is negotiating the sale of its futures unit to a unit of Credit Agricole for $25 million, unnamed sources said.
* A hearing before the Federal Trade Commission will review the proposed merger between Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc.
* Heard on the Street: Media conglomerates from Time Warner to Viacom have been forced to start retrenching. So why does media buccaneer Rupert Murdoch keep buying as though there's no tomorrow?
* Credit Markets: There's no way out. Whether the Federal Reserve jacks up interest rates another notch tomorrow or holds the line, the bond market is in for a bumpy ride.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
